Subject: Pilot credits + commit model inquiry

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked great for our realtime summarization use case. We're exploring a short pilot (6–8 weeks) before committing to anything long-term. Two things we want to validate up front:

- A pilot credit allocation to cover initial traffic (estimate ~2M tokens over 6 weeks) so we can test quality/ops.
- A flexible commit/rebate structure that doesn't lock us into chunky slabs but rewards us as we ramp (we'd prefer a slab-free or continuous rebate approach).

Can Redwood do a milestone-based credit release tied to usage and simple per-token rebates as we hit monthly commit thresholds? Also need a sense for clawback if we don't reach the ramp. Procurement will join on follow-ups.

Thanks,
Emma Zhao
Product Lead — Novapulse

Hi Emma — really glad the demo was useful. Short answer: yes, we can structure a pilot + commit that avoids big discrete slabs and instead uses a continuous per-token rebate plus milestone credit releases. High-level proposal:

1) Pilot credits: Redwood will front 10k USD of pilot credits (applied to hosted per-token billing) to cover initial testing (~2M tokens at your estimated mix).
2) Slab-free rebate: Rather than fixed slabs, we propose a per-token rebate percentage that increases smoothly with cumulative monthly commit. For example: 0–50M tokens/month = base price, then an escalating rebate curve up to a max (we'll attach a sample curve).
3) Milestone credit release: Additional credits (up to $30k) released in two tranches after month-1 and month-2 onboarding checks (ops readiness & integration test results).
4) Clawback terms: If committed ramp isn't met within the agreed 90 days, credits are clawed back pro-rata; reasonable exceptions for force-majeure and agreed pilot metric failures.

I've attached a slab-free term sheet that maps the rebate curve to per-token economics and shows an example P&L for your projected usage. If that aligns, we'll prepare a DocuSign term sheet and include procurement-friendly language for clawback and measurement.

Next steps: can you confirm procurement contact and preferred legal timeline? I can loop in our finance lead (Laura) to expedite.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com

Aditya — added a couple of tactics to consider in the term sheet:

- Tiered per-token percentage (continuous curve) but add a minimum monthly commit to avoid negative margins during long tails (e.g., a $10k/mo minimum after month 3).
- Quality-based holdback: 10% of rebate held for 30 days and released once latency/error SLAs are met — helps align ops.
- Early-exit option: allow Novapulse one early-exit after 60 days with a small unwind fee if certain product metrics fail to meet the pilot spec.

I attached a spreadsheet with a modeled rebate curve and expected unit economics at different usage patterns. Use it to negotiate the exact percentages — I'd avoid giving anything above 25% per-token discount at scale unless we have a multi-quarter commit.

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging — Redwood Inference

Emma, Ryan, procurement — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next steps below: 

1) Clawback formula (short): recovered_credit = max(0, issued_credit * (1 - (actual_cumulative_tokens / committed_cumulative_tokens))). We'll include a worked example in the one-page.
2) Measurement: Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation report (CSV) with token counts by API key, hourly token histogram, 95th percentile token latency, and error-rate (4xx/5xx) by route. These are signed by our finance/ops leads and will be the basis for rebate calculation.
3) Marketing credit: we require a 600–900 word case study + a 30-minute video review call within 90 days post-launch; if Novapulse prefers a shorter format we can reduce the credit to $6k.

Action items:
- We'll circulate a one-page summary + DocuSign-ready term sheet by 2027-07-14 (attached here: commit_term_sheet_docusign.pdf).
- Laura will lead the billing/finance sign-off; Karthik will finalize the exact rebate curve.
- Emma: please confirm the procurement contact name and the target sign date.

If that works, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and loop in legal for a quick review (no complex redlines anticipated).

Regards,
Aditya Rao
